key_insight: AutoResearch can improve a fixed solar-panel segmentation pipeline by letting a coding model iteratively edit training code under a strict compute budget, yielding small but measurable gains in IoU.
engineering_relevance: For photovoltaic inspection workflows, this suggests low-cost automated tuning can outperform a hand-set training schedule without changing the core model architecture.
method: Freeze DeepLabV3-ResNet-50 and optimize only the training program
Run one-hour GPU AutoResearch campaigns with a coding LLM (Gemma 4 12B or Qwen3-8B)
Keep a code change only when validation IoU improves
evidence_signal: Across three campaigns of 24 experiments, all models beat their one-hour baselines, and the best Qwen3-8B setup reached test IoU 0.836 on a frozen real-image split versus 0.833 for the reference GAN-augmented schedule.
watch_item: The retained modifications did not transfer across hardware, so deployment may require revalidation and hardware-specific tuning.
paper_title: Insights from Autoresearch for Solar Panel Segmentation
